name: What is the difference between a room addition and a bump-out?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a room addition and a bump-out, and which is better for Los Angeles homes?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a room addition and a bump-out, and which is better for Los Angeles homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out is typically a smaller-scale expansion of one room, such as extending a kitchen, bedroom, or living area by a few feet. A room addition is usually a larger project that creates a distinct new space with its own function, often including new walls, windows, insulation, and sometimes plumbing or HVAC changes. Bump-outs may be a better fit when the goal is to improve circulation or make an existing room more comfortable without the cost of a full addition. A room addition is better when a homeowner needs a true new bedroom, office, guest room, or suite. In Los Angeles, the decision often comes down to zoning, lot space, budget, and how much new square footage is actually needed. Homeowners should also consider resale value, because a properly designed addition can add more market appeal than a small expansion that only improves one area.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out is a smaller extension of an existing room, while a room addition usually creates a new fully enclosed space such as a bedroom, office, or suite. Bump-outs are often cheaper and faster, but room additions provide more usable square footage and more flexible layouts.
